lines: Open Workforce and choose Work entries.
The table separates the worker, hours, hours type, establishment,
context and approval status.
In this training department, the existing two-hour entry shows No under Approved.
We will create a separate example and follow it from an unapproved
save to a verified approved result.
An administrator needs the appropriate workforce access for these controls.
The earlier example remains unchanged.
Select Add work entry.
In the form, the worker is Matthew Casey.
Set Date to November first, twenty twenty-six, enter one
point two five Hours, and choose Standby under Hours type.
Select the training establishment appropriate to the example.
These fields describe this individual work entry.
Check the worker, date, quantity and hours type together before continuing, so the
approval will refer to the intended row.
Scroll to the bottom of the form.
External source and External id provide references for this example.
Leave the Approved checkbox clear for the first save.
The Approved payroll cost field is also blank in this exercise.
Select Save, then find the new row with the context TRAINING
ONLY, Approval exercise.
Its date, one point two five hours and Standby type are visible,
and Approved still reads No.
This returned row confirms the initial saved state.
Use the pencil control at the right of the new exercise row to reopen it.
Scroll to Approved and select the checkbox.
In this view, the table on the left still shows the earlier
saved value, No, while the form checkbox on the right is selected.
The form change still needs to be saved.
Confirm that this is the intended training entry, then select Save
to store its approval status.
Reload the Work entries page.
The new exercise row now shows Yes under Approved.
The worker, date, one point two five hours and Standby type
remain visible on that same row.
The earlier two-hour entry still shows No.
Compare the complete row when reviewing an approval, rather than reading a
Yes value without its worker and date.
The Approved payroll cost column remains blank for this software exercise.
Use the two date fields above the table to focus the review.
Set both boundaries to November first, twenty twenty-six, then select Filter.
The returned table contains the single exercise entry for that
date, including its Standby hours, context and Yes approval value.
Changing the date fields alone does not refresh this table; the Filter
button applies the selected range.
Check those boundaries when a saved entry seems to be missing from the list.
This workflow gives a department a visible saved approval status
for a particular work entry.
A security supervisor can review patrol standby time, a search-and-rescue
coordinator can review an exercise entry, and a community paramedicine
or mental health response team can review its recorded work.
Wildland contractors, industrial response teams, and fire and E M S
departments can use the same worker, date, hours type and context checks.
Agree who reviews entries, then verify the saved result
in the appropriate date range.
